note: Tolkien's notes on the map Pauline Baynes drew in 1969-70, and Baynes's own working notes beside them. The archive publishes the WORDS, on the authority of the books that carry them, and does not reproduce her map. Where only the marked sheet witnesses a note it is marked [EXT], not [C].

notes.subject: Eryn Vorn
notes.text: Eryn Vorn [Black Forest] — a forest region of dark pine trees
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi; UT, The Rivers and Beacon-hills of Gondor

notes.subject: Lond Daer
notes.text: Lond Daer [ruins]
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi; UT, The Rivers and Beacon-hills of Gondor

notes.subject: Drúwaith Iaur
notes.text: Drúwaith Iaur [Old Pukel-land]
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi; UT, The Drúedain, editor's note 13

notes.subject: Edhellond
notes.text: Edhellond — the Elf-haven at the mouth of the Morthond, placed on the map at Tolkien's instruction
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi; UT, The History of Galadriel and Celeborn

notes.subject: Framsburg
notes.text: Framsburg — near the Éothéod, at the head of Anduin
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi

notes.subject: Éothéod
notes.text: Éothéod — the northern land of the horse-folk before Rohan
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi; UT, Cirion and Eorl

notes.subject: Dorwinion
notes.text: Dorwinion — placed on the north-western shore of the Sea of Rhûn
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi

notes.subject: Andrast
notes.text: Andrast — the name for the cape the sheet letters Cape Andrast
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi

notes.subject: Enedwaith
notes.text: sparse woodland could be represented where I put pencil shade
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi

notes.subject: Swanfleet
notes.text: marshes should be under and about the junction of Swanfleet and Hoarwell. The upper part of the Swanfleet is called Glanduin [Boundary River]. Apply Swanfleet to the lower part and if possible place R. Glanduin near mountains
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi; UT, The Rivers and Beacon-hills of Gondor

notes.subject: Tumladen (Gondor)
notes.text: if possible the vale between Celos and Sirith should be lettered Tumladen
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings, pp. lxiii–lxvi

notes.subject: Carnen
notes.text: Carnen is mentioned — the red river
notes.cite: LotR, App. A III; RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings

notes.subject: Celduin
notes.text: Celduin — the River Running, named beside the red river
notes.cite: LotR, App. A III

notes.subject: Erui
notes.text: Erui — the first of the streams of Lebennin
notes.cite: LotR, App. A; RC

notes.subject: Hobbiton
notes.text: Hobbiton — marked on the sheet in Tolkien's own ink
notes.cite: LotR, I

notes.subject: Isengard
notes.text: Isengard — marked on the sheet in Tolkien's own ink
notes.cite: LotR, III

notes.subject: Hobbiton
notes.text: Hobbiton is assumed to be approx at latitude of Oxford. The green vertical line is marked at distances of 100 miles (2cms to map scale). So you can roughly judge the climate and Fauna/Flora etc.
notes.cite: Letters, no. 294; RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings

notes.subject: Minas Tirith
notes.text: Minas Tirith is about a latitude of Ravenna (but is 900 miles east of Hobbiton, more near Belgrade)
notes.cite: Letters, no. 294; RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings

notes.subject: the foot of the sheet
notes.text: Bottom of the Map (400 miles) is about a latitude of Jerusalem
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings

notes.subject: Umbar
notes.text: Umbar and the City of the Corsairs — about that of Cyprus
notes.cite: RC, The Maps of The Lord of the Rings

notes.subject: the sheet
notes.text: green horizontal is also marked in 100 mile intervals
notes.cite: the transcription of the marked sheet

notes.subject: the Elves
notes.text: Elven ships small, white or grey
notes.cite: the transcription of the marked sheet

notes.subject: Gondor
notes.text: Númenórean (Gondor) ships black and silver
notes.cite: the transcription of the marked sheet

notes.subject: the Corsairs of Umbar
notes.text: Corsairs had red sails with black star or eye
notes.cite: the transcription of the marked sheet

notes.subject: the Corsairs of Umbar
notes.text: vessels of varying sizes from 3 masted to single
notes.cite: the transcription of the marked sheet

notes.subject: Rhovanion
notes.text: Plains of Rhovanion between Mirkwood, Rhûn and Mordor had many wild kine and wild horses
notes.cite: the transcription of the marked sheet

notes.subject: Harad
notes.text: Elephants appear in the great battle outside Minas Tirith (as they did in Italy under Pyrrhus) but they could be in place in the blank spaces of Harad, also camels
notes.cite: LotR, IV.4 and V.6, for the mûmakil; the rest from the marked sheet

notes.subject: Ephel Dúath
notes.text: indigo

notes.subject: the White Mountains
notes.text: blue and purple peaks of jet topped with snow
notes.cite: the transcription of the marked sheet

notes.subject: the Brown Lands
notes.text: desolate, black brown
notes.cite: the transcription of the marked sheet

notes.subject: Orthanc
notes.text: tower of stone
notes.cite: the transcription of the marked sheet

notes.subject: the Teeth of Mordor
notes.text: 2 towers, teeth of Mordor — haunted pass

notes.subject: the Corsairs of Umbar
notes.text: 9 weatherbeaten galleons, 7 of which had a single white star on main sail, all black, 5 masted — as large a pre-steam vessel as can be drawn, ie Columbus type
notes.cite: the transcription of the marked sheet

notes.subject: the Elves
notes.text: single masted elven vessels, white or grey sail; small boats any shape going eastwards
